claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: In C. elegans hermaphrodites, 60 ciliated and 12 non-ciliated neurons perform most sensory functions.
claims.source: In C. elegans hermaphrodites, 60 ciliated and 12 non-ciliated neurons perform most sensory functions (White et al., 1986).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to White et al., 1986.

claims.claim: Individual ablation of ASJ and AWA, and joint ablation of URX, AQR, and PQR reduced peroxide resistance by up to 16%.
claims.source: whereas individual ablation of ASJ and AWA, and joint ablation of URX, AQR, and PQR reduced peroxide resistance by up to 16% (Figure 1A–B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A–B.

claims.claim: Ablation of ADF, ADL, ASE, ASH, AWB, OLL, and joint ablation of ALM, PLM, AVM, PVM, FLP, and PVD did not affect peroxide resistance.
claims.source: The remainder of the neurons tested—ADF, ADL, ASE, ASH, AWB, OLL, and joint ablation of ALM, PLM, AVM, PVM, FLP, and PVD—did not affect peroxide resistance (Figure 1A and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–G, and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–G, and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: ASI neurons sense taste and temperature.
claims.source: Among all neuronal ablations tested, ablation of ASI, a pair of neurons that sense taste and temperature, caused the largest increase in peroxide resistance (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim draws from established knowledge about ASI neuron function.

claims.claim: DAF-7 is a transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) hormone that regulates feeding, development, metabolism, and lifespan.
claims.source: DAF-7 (Meisel et al., 2014; Ren et al., 1996), a transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) hormone that regulates feeding, development, metabolism, and lifespan (Dalfó et al., 2012; Greer et al., 2008; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dalfó et al., 2012; Greer et al., 2008; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007.

claims.claim: daf-7(ok3125) null and daf-7(e1372) loss-of-function mutations increased peroxide resistance two-fold relative to wild-type controls.
claims.source: We found that daf-7(ok3125) null and daf-7(e1372) loss-of-function mutations increased peroxide resistance two-fold relative to wild-type controls (Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D, and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D, and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Reintroducing the daf-7(+) gene into daf-7(ok3125) mutants restored peroxide resistance to wild-type levels.
claims.source: Reintroducing the daf-7(+) gene into daf-7(ok3125) mutants restored peroxide resistance to wild-type levels (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Expression of daf-7(+) only in the ASI neurons was sufficient to reduce the peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) mutants to wild-type levels.
claims.source: Moreover, expression of daf-7(+) only in the ASI neurons was sufficient to reduce the peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) mutants to wild-type levels (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Expression of daf-7(+) only in ASJ rescued the increased peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) mutants.
claims.source: and expression of daf-7(+) only in ASJ rescued the increased peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) mutants (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: ASI neurons are the source of DAF-7 that regulates the nematode's peroxide resistance.
claims.source: Because ablation of ASI increased peroxide resistance but ablation of ASJ did not (Figure 1A), we reason that ASI neurons are the source of DAF-7 that regulates the nematode's peroxide resistance.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on logical inference from the experimental data.

claims.claim: daf-7(ok3125) mutants had similar survival to wild-type animals in 5 mM arsenite, 25 mM dithiothreitol, and 75 mM paraquat.
claims.source: Compared with wild-type animals, daf-7(ok3125) mutants had similar survival in 5 mM arsenite, 25 mM dithiothreitol, and 75 mM paraquat (Figure 2A and E–G, and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and E–G, and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: The DAF-7/TGFβ signal from ASI is a specific regulator of peroxide resistance in the worm.
claims.source: Therefore, the DAF-7/TGFβ signal from ASI is a specific regulator of peroxide resistance in the worm.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing specificity to peroxide resistance.

claims.claim: DAF-7/TGFβ signals via the Type 1 TGFβ receptor DAF-1.
claims.source: DAF-7/TGFβ signals via the Type 1 TGFβ receptor DAF-1 (Georgi et al., 1990) to regulate multiple downstream processes (Dalfó et al., 2012; Greer et al., 2008; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Georgi et al., 1990; Dalfó et al., 2012; Greer et al., 2008; Ren et al., 1996; Shaw et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Signaling through the DAF-1 receptor inactivates the transcriptional activity of a complex between the receptor-associated coSMAD, DAF-3, and the Sno/Ski factor, DAF-5.
claims.source: Signaling through the DAF-1 receptor inactivates the transcriptional activity of a complex between the receptor-associated coSMAD, DAF-3, and the Sno/Ski factor, DAF-5 (da Graca, 2004; Patterson et al., 1997; Tewari et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to da Graca, 2004; Patterson et al., 1997; Tewari et al., 2004.

claims.claim: The increase in peroxide resistance of daf-7 and daf-1 mutants was almost completely abrogated by null or loss-of-function mutations in either daf-3 or daf-5.
claims.source: and the increase in peroxide resistance of daf-7 and daf-1 mutants was almost completely abrogated by null or loss-of-function mutations in either daf-3 or daf-5 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C, and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C, and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: The daf-3(mgDf90) null mutation suppressed the increase in peroxide resistance of ASI-ablated worms.
claims.source: The daf-3(mgDf90) null mutation also suppressed the increase in peroxide resistance of ASI-ablated worms (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: The ASI neurons normally function to lower peroxide resistance in the worm using a canonical TGFβ signaling pathway.
claims.source: Therefore, the ASI neurons normally function to lower peroxide resistance in the worm using a canonical TGFβ signaling pathway.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on the TGFβ signaling pathway.

claims.claim: Pan-neuronal expression of daf-1(+) with the egl-3 promoter lowered peroxide resistance in daf-1 mutants to the same extent as did expressing daf-1(+) with the endogenous daf-1 promoter.
claims.source: Pan-neuronal expression of daf-1(+) with the egl-3 promoter lowered peroxide resistance in daf-1 mutants to the same extent as did expressing daf-1(+) with the endogenous daf-1 promoter (Figure 3D–E, and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D–E, and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: Directed daf-1(+) expression in nine pharyngeal neurons using the glr-7 promoter did not affect peroxide resistance.
claims.source: while directed daf-1(+) expression in nine pharyngeal neurons using the glr-7 promoter did not affect peroxide resistance (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: The flp-1 promoter is active only in the two AVK interneurons.
claims.source: The flp-1 promoter is active only in the two AVK interneurons (Greer et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Greer et al., 2008.

claims.claim: DAF-1 functions redundantly in AVK interneurons and at least two other separate sets of neurons to lower the nematode's peroxide resistance.
claims.source: We conclude that DAF-1 functions redundantly in AVK interneurons and at least two other separate sets of neurons to lower the nematode's peroxide resistance.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on daf-1 expression patterns.

claims.claim: Restoring daf-3(+) expression with the tdc-1 promoter was not sufficient to increase peroxide resistance in daf-1; daf-3 double mutants.
claims.source: Confirming our prediction, we found that restoring daf-3(+) expression with the tdc-1 promoter was not sufficient to increase peroxide resistance in daf-1; daf-3 double mutants (Figure 3K, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F, and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3K, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F, and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: The peroxide resistance of daf-1; daf-3 double mutants increased upon restoring daf-3(+) expression in all four DAF-1-sufficiency sets of neurons with a daf-1 promoter.
claims.source: In contrast, the peroxide resistance of daf-1; daf-3 double mutants increased upon restoring daf-3(+) expression in all four DAF-1-sufficiency sets of neurons with a daf-1 promoter (Figure 3J and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: DAF-7 regulates dauer-larva formation via the nuclear hormone receptor DAF-12.
claims.source: DAF-7 regulates dauer-larva formation via the nuclear hormone receptor DAF-12, which is the main switch driving the choice of reproductive growth or dauer arrest (Antebi et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Antebi et al., 2000.

claims.claim: The daf-12(rh61rh411) null mutation did not suppress the increased peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) null adults.
claims.source: but the daf-12(rh61rh411) null mutation did not suppress the increased peroxide resistance of daf-7(ok3125) null adults (Figure 4B and Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Supplementary file 4.

claims.claim: The metabotropic glutamate receptors mgl-1 and mgl-3 are necessary for the increase in fat storage upon DAF-7-pathway inhibition.
claims.source: The metabotropic glutamate receptors mgl-1 and mgl-3 are necessary for the increase in fat storage upon DAF-7-pathway inhibition (Greer et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Greer et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Null mutations in either or both mgl-1 and mgl-3 did not affect peroxide resistance in daf-1 mutants.
claims.source: However, null mutations in either or both of these mgl genes did not affect peroxide resistance in daf-1 mutants (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 4.

claims.claim: Germline size is reduced upon DAF-7-pathway inhibition.
claims.source: Germline size is reduced upon DAF-7-pathway inhibition (Dalfó et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dalfó et al., 2012.

claims.claim: Germline-ablated mes-1(ok2467) mutants showed a 57% increase in peroxide resistance compared to their fertile mes-1(ok2467) mutant siblings.
claims.source: Germline-ablated mes-1(ok2467) mutants showed a 57% increase in peroxide resistance compared to their fertile mes-1(ok2467) mutant siblings (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 4), consistent with previous studies (Steinbaugh et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 4, and cited from Steinbaugh et al., 2015.

claims.claim: daf-1(m40) increased peroxide resistance in both germline-ablated and fertile mes-1 mutants.
claims.source: However, daf-1(m40) increased peroxide resistance in both germline-ablated and fertile mes-1 mutants (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 4.

claims.claim: daf-3(mgDf90) did not affect peroxide resistance in germline-ablated mes-1 mutants.
claims.source: In addition, daf-3(mgDf90) did not affect peroxide resistance in germline-ablated mes-1 mutants (Figure 4E and Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and Supplementary file 4.

claims.claim: DAF-1 and the germline regulate peroxide resistance via independent mechanisms.
claims.source: Therefore, DAF-1 and the germline regulate peroxide resistance via independent mechanisms.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on daf-1 and germline effects.

claims.claim: DAF-7-pathway signaling lowers lifespan by promoting insulin/IGF1 receptor signaling.
claims.source: DAF-7-pathway signaling lowers lifespan by promoting insulin/IGF1 receptor signaling (Shaw et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shaw et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Transcription of at least 11 of the 40 insulin/IGF1 genes in the genome is repressed by the DAF-3/coSMAD in response to lower levels of DAF-7 and DAF-1 signaling.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that transcription of at least 11 of the 40 insulin/IGF1 genes in the genome is repressed by the DAF-3/coSMAD in response to lower levels of DAF-7 and DAF-1 signaling (Liu et al., 2004; Narasimhan et al., 2011; Shaw et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2004; Narasimhan et al., 2011; Shaw et al., 2007.

claims.claim: The daf-2(e1370) strong loss-of-function mutation increased peroxide resistance about three-fold.
claims.source: The daf-2(e1370) strong loss-of-function mutation increased peroxide resistance about three-fold (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 5), consistent with previous findings (Tullet et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 5, and cited from Tullet et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Double mutants of daf-1(m40) and daf-2(e1370) had higher peroxide resistance than the respective single mutants.
claims.source: Double mutants of daf-1(m40) and daf-2(e1370) had higher peroxide resistance than the respective single mutants (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: DAF-16 is necessary for the increase in lifespan and most other phenotypes of mutants with reduced signaling by the DAF-2 insulin/IGF1 receptor.
claims.source: DAF-16 is necessary for the increase in lifespan and most other phenotypes of mutants with reduced signaling by the DAF-2 insulin/IGF1 receptor (Kenyon et al., 1993; Lin et al., 1997; Ogg et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kenyon et al., 1993; Lin et al., 1997; Ogg et al., 1997.

claims.claim: DAF-16 was necessary for the increase in peroxide resistance of an ins-4 ins-5 ins-6; daf-28 quadruple mutant.
claims.source: and for the increase in peroxide resistance of an ins-4 ins-5 ins-6; daf-28 quadruple mutant (Figure 5D and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: The daf-16(mu86) null mutation decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-7(e1372) and daf-1(m40) mutants by nearly 50%.
claims.source: The daf-16(mu86) null mutation decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-7(e1372) and daf-1(m40) mutants by nearly 50%, but caused only a small peroxide resistance reduction in wild-type nematodes (Figure 5E–F, and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E–F, and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: Regulation of peroxide resistance by the DAF-7/TGFβ signaling pathway is, in part, dependent on the DAF-16/FOXO transcription factor.
claims.source: Therefore, regulation of peroxide resistance by the DAF-7/TGFβ signaling pathway is, in part, dependent on the DAF-16/FOXO transcription factor.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on DAF-16 dependence.

claims.claim: Like DAF-16, the NRF orthologue SKN-1 and the TFEB orthologue HLH-30 are activated in response to reduced DAF-2 signaling.
claims.source: Like DAF-16, the NRF orthologue SKN-1 and the TFEB orthologue HLH-30 are activated in response to reduced DAF-2 signaling (Lin et al., 2018; Tullet et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2018; Tullet et al., 2008.

claims.claim: The peroxide resistance of daf-1(m40) hlh-30(tm1978) double mutants was identical to that of daf-1 single mutants.
claims.source: The peroxide resistance of daf-1(m40) hlh-30(tm1978) double mutants was identical to that of daf-1 single mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: Knockdown of skn-1 via RNA interference decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-1(m40) mutants by 30% but did not affect peroxide resistance in wild-type nematodes.
claims.source: Knockdown of skn-1 via RNA interference (RNAi) decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-1(m40) mutants by 30% but did not affect peroxide resistance in wild-type nematodes (Figure 5G and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: RNAi of skn-1 decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-16; daf-1 double mutants.
claims.source: RNAi of skn-1 also decreased the peroxide resistance of daf-16; daf-1 double mutants, suggesting that DAF-16 and SKN-1 functioned in a non-overlapping manner to promote peroxide resistance in daf-1(m40) mutants (Figure 5H and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: Restoring daf-16(+) expression only in the intestine increased peroxide resistance in daf-16; daf-1 double mutants.
claims.source: Restoring daf-16(+) expression only in the intestine increased peroxide resistance, albeit to a lesser extent than did re-expressing daf-16(+) with the endogenous daf-16 promoter (Figure 5J and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5J and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: Restoring daf-16(+) in body-wall muscles had no effect on peroxide resistance in daf-16; daf-1 double mutants.
claims.source: while restoring daf-16(+) in body-wall muscles had no effect (Figure 5L and Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5L and Supplementary file 5.

claims.claim: The DAF-16/FOXO transcription factor functions in the intestine and neurons to increase the nematode's peroxide resistance when DAF-3/coSMAD is active due to reduced DAF-1 function.
claims.source: Therefore, the DAF-16/FOXO transcription factor functions in the intestine and neurons to increase the nematode's peroxide resistance when DAF-3/coSMAD is active due to reduced DAF-1 function (Figure 5N).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on tissue-specific daf-16 rescue.

claims.claim: Relative to wild-type animals, daf-7(ok3125) null mutants decreased the expression of 3641 genes and increased the expression of 3229 genes (q value < 0.001).
claims.source: Relative to wild-type animals, daf-7(ok3125) null mutants decreased the expression of 3641 genes and increased the expression of 3229 genes (q value < 0.001) (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mRNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The 1267 genes downregulated more than four-fold in daf-7(ok3125) mutants were associated with reproduction and with expression in the germline.
claims.source: The 1267 genes downregulated more than four-fold in daf-7(ok3125) mutants were associated with reproduction and with expression in the germline, while the 594 genes upregulated more than four-fold in daf-7(ok3125) mutants were associated with defense and immune responses and with expression in the intestine (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The daf-7(ok3125) mutation increased the expression of genes upregulated by skn-1(+) in wild type animals.
claims.source: The daf-7(ok3125) mutation increased the expression of genes upregulated by skn-1(+) in wild type animals (Oliveira et al., 2009) and in daf-2(-) mutants (Ewald et al., 2015; Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Supplementary file 6, and cited from Oliveira et al., 2009 and Ewald et al., 2015.

claims.claim: DAF-7/TGFβ represses the induction of direct DAF-16 and SKN-1 target genes.
claims.source: Together, these findings suggest that DAF-7/TGFβ represses the induction of direct DAF-16 and SKN-1 target genes.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the transcriptomic data.

claims.claim: The tyrosine decarboxylase TDC-1 and the tyramine β-hydroxylase TBH-1 are each necessary for the feeding defect of daf-1 mutants.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that the tyrosine decarboxylase TDC-1 and the tyramine β-hydroxylase TBH-1—biosynthetic enzymes for the neurotransmitters tyramine and octopamine, respectively—are each necessary for the feeding defect of daf-1 mutants as daf-1;tdc-1 and daf-1;tbh-1 double mutants have normal feeding behaviors (Greer et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Greer et al., 2008.

claims.claim: tbh-1 and tdc-1 null mutations did not suppress the increased peroxide resistance of daf-1 mutants.
claims.source: Surprisingly, despite restoring normal feeding to daf-1 mutants, tbh-1 and tdc-1 null mutations did not suppress the increased peroxide resistance of daf-1 mutants (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, and Supplementary file 7).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, and Supplementary file 7.

claims.claim: The E. coli concentration before the assay had a dose-dependent effect on peroxide resistance.
claims.source: We transferred nematodes to plates with different concentrations of E. coli for 24 hr prior to the start of the peroxide resistance assay and found that the E. coli concentration before the assay had a dose-dependent effect on peroxide resistance (Figure 7B and Supplementary file 7).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and Supplementary file 7.

claims.claim: The eat-2(ad1116) loss-of-function mutation decreased peroxide resistance by 25% relative to wild-type animals.
claims.source: The eat-2(ad1116) loss-of-function mutation, which causes a strong feeding defect (Figure 7E), decreased peroxide resistance by 25% relative to wild-type animals (Figure 7D and Supplementary file 7).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D and Supplementary file 7.

claims.claim: Impaired feeding leads to decreased peroxide resistance.
claims.source: Therefore, impaired feeding leads to decreased peroxide resistance.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data on eat-2 mutants.

claims.claim: DAF-3 is activated in response to reduced feeding, leading to an increase in peroxide resistance.
claims.source: We propose that DAF-3 is activated in response to reduced feeding, leading to an increase in peroxide resistance.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: ASI neurons induce daf-7 gene expression in a TAX-4-activity-dependent manner.
claims.source: and induce daf-7 gene expression in a TAX-4-activity-dependent manner (Chang et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chang et al., 2006.

claims.claim: ASI neurons lower daf-7 gene expression in response to starvation and low E. coli concentrations.
claims.source: and lower daf-7 gene expression in response to starvation and low E. coli concentrations (Entchev et al., 2015; Ren et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Entchev et al., 2015; Ren et al., 1996.

claims.claim: E. coli uses several scavenging systems to degrade hydrogen peroxide.
claims.source: This bacterium uses several scavenging systems to degrade hydrogen peroxide (Mishra and Imlay, 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mishra and Imlay, 2012.

claims.claim: The two E. coli catalases, KatG and KatE, are the predominant scavengers of hydrogen peroxide in the environment.
claims.source: The two E. coli catalases, KatG and KatE, are the predominant scavengers of hydrogen peroxide in the environment, and the peroxiredoxin, AhpCF, plays a minor role (Seaver and Imlay, 2001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Seaver and Imlay, 2001.

claims.claim: The E. coli MG1655 parental wild-type strain was protective against hydrogen peroxide killing of C. elegans.
claims.source: whereas the E. coli MG1655 parental wild-type strain was protective (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claims.claim: E. coli protects C. elegans from hydrogen peroxide killing because it expresses catalases that efficiently deplete hydrogen peroxide from the environment.
claims.source: We propose that E. coli protects C. elegans from hydrogen peroxide killing because it expresses catalases that efficiently deplete hydrogen peroxide from the environment, creating a local environment where hydrogen peroxide is not a threat to C. elegans.
claims.evidence: This is a proposal based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: daf-7(ok3125) increased the nematode's hydrogen peroxide resistance over two-fold relative to wild-type nematodes in assays with the catalase mutant E. coli JI377 strain.
claims.source: In assays with the catalase mutant E. coli JI377 strain, we found that daf-7(ok3125) increased the nematode's hydrogen peroxide resistance over two-fold relative to wild-type nematodes (Figure 8B and Supplementary file 8).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B and Supplementary file 8.

claims.claim: ASI-ablation increased hydrogen peroxide resistance in assays with E. coli JI377.
claims.source: ASI-ablation also increased hydrogen peroxide resistance in assays with E. coli JI377 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 8).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 8.

claims.claim: The C. elegans genome contains three catalase genes in tandem—two newly duplicated cytosolic catalases, ctl-1 and ctl-3, and a peroxisomal catalase, ctl-2.
claims.source: The C. elegans genome contains three catalase genes in tandem—two-newly duplicated cytosolic catalases, ctl-1 and ctl-3, and a peroxisomal catalase, ctl-2—which are the nematode orthologues of the two E. coli catalases, KatG and KatE (Petriv and Rachubinski, 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Petriv and Rachubinski, 2004.

claims.claim: ctl-1 and ctl-2 were induced by the daf-7(ok3125) mutation.
claims.source: In our mRNA-seq analysis we found that ctl-1 and ctl-2 were induced by the daf-7(ok3125) mutation (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mRNA-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Catalase mRNA and protein expression increase in a DAF-16-dependent manner when DAF-2 signaling is reduced.
claims.source: and their mRNA and protein expression increase in a DAF-16-dependent manner when DAF-2 signaling is reduced (Dong et al., 2007; McElwee et al., 2003; Murphy et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dong et al., 2007; McElwee et al., 2003; Murphy et al., 2003.

claims.claim: ctl-1/2/3 overexpression more than doubled C. elegans hydrogen peroxide resistance in assays with E. coli JI377.
claims.source: We found that ctl-1/2/3 overexpression, which increases catalase activity ten-fold (Doonan et al., 2008), more than doubled C. elegans hydrogen peroxide resistance in assays with E. coli JI377 (Figure 8C and Supplementary file 8).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C and Supplementary file 8, and cited from Doonan et al., 2008.

claims.claim: The peroxisomal catalase ctl-2(ok1137) null mutation did not suppress the increased hydrogen peroxide resistance of daf-1(m40) mutants.
claims.source: but the peroxisomal catalase ctl-2(ok1137) null mutation did not (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 8).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 8.

claims.claim: The increase in hydrogen peroxide resistance of daf-1 mutants is mediated in part by the CTL-1 cytosolic catalase.

results.result: Ten classes of sensory neurons regulate peroxide resistance in C. elegans. Mutations affecting sensory cilia (osm-5) and sensory transduction (tax-2, tax-4) increased peroxide resistance by 45-124%. Systematic ablation of specific sensory neurons identified seven classes that normally reduce peroxide resistance (ASI, ASG, ASK, AFD, AWC, IL2, and ADE/PDE/CEP) and three classes that increase it (ASJ, AWA, and URX/AQR/PQR).
results.evaluation: Claims C19, C24, C26, C29, and C30 are well-supported by systematic genetic ablation experiments shown in Figure 1 with appropriate controls and statistical analyses. The experimental design is rigorous, covering 54 of 72 sensory neurons, and the results are internally consistent with multiple independent measurements.

results.result: ASI sensory neurons regulate peroxide resistance via DAF-7/TGFβ signaling. Loss-of-function mutations in daf-7 increased peroxide resistance two-fold, which was rescued by reintroducing daf-7(+) specifically in ASI neurons. This regulation is specific to peroxide resistance, as daf-7 mutants showed normal survival to arsenite, paraquat, and dithiothreitol.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C41 are strongly supported by genetic rescue experiments (C35, C36, C38) and specificity controls (C40). The tissue-specific rescue experiments provide compelling evidence that ASI is the relevant source of DAF-7 for peroxide resistance regulation. The specificity to peroxide versus other stressors strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: DAF-7/TGFβ signals through a canonical pathway involving DAF-1 receptor and DAF-3/DAF-5 transcriptional complex. DAF-1 functions redundantly in multiple sets of interneurons (including AVK and at least two other sets) to regulate peroxide resistance. DAF-3 must be active in all DAF-1-sufficiency sets of neurons to increase peroxide resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C55 are supported by comprehensive genetic epistasis experiments and tissue-specific rescue studies. The redundant function of DAF-1 in multiple neuronal sets is demonstrated through promoter-specific expression experiments (C48, C53). The requirement for DAF-3 activity in all DAF-1-sufficiency sets (C54, C55) is logically consistent with the proposed model.

results.result: DAF-7/TGFβ regulation of peroxide resistance is independent of pathways controlling dauer formation (DAF-12), fat storage (MGL-1/MGL-3), and germline-mediated effects. Double mutant analyses show that daf-1 and germline ablation independently increase peroxide resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C58, C60, C63-C65 are supported by appropriate double mutant analyses showing independence of pathways. The genetic logic is sound: if pathways were dependent, suppression would be observed in double mutants, but additive or independent effects were seen instead. This establishes pathway specificity.

results.result: DAF-7/TGFβ signaling regulates peroxide resistance partially through the insulin/IGF1 receptor DAF-2 and the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16. Loss of daf-2 increased peroxide resistance three-fold, and daf-16 was necessary for increased peroxide resistance in daf-2 mutants and partially necessary in daf-1 mutants (reducing resistance by ~50%).
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C75 are supported by genetic epistasis experiments. The partial suppression of daf-1 phenotypes by daf-16 (C74) appropriately supports the conclusion of partial dependence (C75). The additive effects of daf-1 and daf-2 mutations (C70) suggest overlapping but not identical mechanisms, consistent with the partial dependence model.

results.result: SKN-1/NRF transcription factor acts independently of DAF-16 to promote peroxide resistance in daf-1 mutants. RNAi knockdown of skn-1 reduced peroxide resistance of daf-1 mutants by 30% and also reduced resistance in daf-16; daf-1 double mutants, while hlh-30 had no effect.
results.evaluation: Claims C78, C79, and C77 are supported by RNAi experiments showing non-overlapping function of SKN-1 and DAF-16. The observation that skn-1 RNAi affects daf-16; daf-1 double mutants (C79) provides strong evidence for independent pathways. The negative result with hlh-30 (C77) appropriately rules out this alternative transcription factor.

results.result: DAF-16/FOXO functions in the intestine and neurons to increase peroxide resistance when DAF-1 signaling is reduced. Tissue-specific rescue experiments showed that restoring daf-16(+) in the intestine partially rescued peroxide resistance, while restoration in body-wall muscles had no effect.
results.evaluation: Claims C80, C82, and C83 are supported by tissue-specific rescue experiments using appropriate promoters. The partial rescue with intestinal expression (C80) and lack of rescue with muscle expression (C82) provide clear evidence for tissue-specific function. The conclusion (C83) appropriately integrates these findings.

results.result: Loss of daf-7 causes widespread transcriptional changes, with 3641 genes downregulated and 3229 genes upregulated. Downregulated genes are associated with reproduction and germline expression, while upregulated genes are associated with defense responses and intestinal expression. The daf-7 mutation increases expression of SKN-1 and DAF-16 target genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C88 are supported by mRNA-seq data with appropriate statistical thresholds (q < 0.001) and biological replicates. The Gene Ontology analysis (C85) and comparison to known SKN-1 and DAF-16 targets (C86) provide functional validation of the transcriptomic changes. The inference about DAF-7 repressing these targets (C88) is reasonable given the genetic epistasis data.

results.result: Food ingestion regulates peroxide resistance independently of the feeding defect in daf-1 mutants. E. coli concentration before the assay has a dose-dependent effect on peroxide resistance. The eat-2 feeding-defective mutation decreased peroxide resistance by 25%, and DAF-3 is proposed to be activated in response to reduced feeding.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C94 are supported by experimental data, but C96 is explicitly labeled as a speculative proposal. While the data on feeding effects (C91, C93) are solid, the mechanistic proposal about DAF-3 activation (C96) lacks direct experimental validation. The relationship between feeding and DAF-3 activity requires additional experiments to confirm.

results.result: E. coli catalases protect C. elegans from hydrogen peroxide. Wild-type E. coli MG1655 protected nematodes from hydrogen peroxide killing, while catalase-deficient E. coli JI377 did not. In assays with catalase-deficient E. coli, daf-7 mutants and ASI-ablated animals showed increased hydrogen peroxide resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C106-C109 are supported by experiments using defined E. coli strains with and without catalase activity. The use of the JI377 triple mutant (lacking KatG, KatE, and AhpCF) provides a clean genetic background to test the role of bacterial catalases. The observation that daf-7 effects are revealed only with catalase-deficient bacteria (C108, C109) is logically consistent with the freeloading model.

results.result: The DAF-7/TGFβ pathway downregulates C. elegans catalase expression, particularly ctl-1, partly via DAF-16. The ctl-1 and ctl-2 genes were induced by daf-7 mutation in mRNA-seq. Overexpression of all three catalases doubled hydrogen peroxide resistance. The ctl-1 null mutation partially suppressed increased resistance in daf-1 mutants. ctl-1 mRNA and protein expression were elevated in daf-1 mutants in a partially DAF-16-dependent manner.
results.evaluation: Claims C111, C114, C117-C119, C121-C122 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: transcriptomics (C111), overexpression (C114), genetic epistasis (C117), qRT-PCR (C118, C119), and microscopy (C121). The partial DAF-16 dependence (C119) is appropriately demonstrated by the small but significant reduction in ctl-1 expression in daf-16; daf-1 double mutants. The conclusion (C122) integrates these findings appropriately.
